summary.text: The front matter of the Global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 (WHO, 2021), with ISBNs, licence terms and the table of contents. It includes acknowledgements describing the two-year consultation that led to adoption by the Seventy-third World Health Assembly. Based on the shown end, it also contains the introduction tracing the strategy to earlier eHealth and digital health resolutions, with notes citing sources such as the WHO–ITU National eHealth Strategy Toolkit.

sections.title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES – SHAPING THE FUTURE OF GLOBAL HEALTH

summary.text: Describes how digital technologies are shaping global health, citing the 2030 Agenda and UN reviews of the World Summit on the Information Society. It argues that digital and frontier technologies can help reach WHO's triple billion targets and improve diagnosis, treatment and self-care. It notes that many countries still need support for national strategies and that digital health should be ethical, safe, equitable and interoperable.

sections.extract: THE FUTURE OF GLOBAL HEALTH The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development1 highlights that the spread of information and communications technology and global interconnectedness has great potential to accelerate human progress, to bridge the digital divide and to develop knowledge societies. The outcome document of the high-level meeting of the United Nations General Assembly on the overall review of the implementation

sections.title: VISION

summary.text: Sets out the strategy's vision of better health for everyone through appropriate, affordable and sustainable person-centred digital health solutions, including for epidemics and pandemics. It lists the conditions under which digital health will be valued and calls for evidence on global solutions in different country contexts.

sections.extract: VISION The vision of the global strategy is to improve health for everyone, everywhere by accelerating the development and adoption of appropriate, accessible, affordable, scalable and sustainable person- centric digital health solutions to prevent, detect and respond to epidemics and pandemics, developing infrastructure and applications that enable countries to use health data to promote health and well-being, and

sections.title: PURPOSE

summary.text: States the strategy's purpose of strengthening health systems by applying digital technologies for patients, professionals, providers and industry, and defines digital health broadly to include eHealth and emerging fields. It stresses health data protection, interoperability and appropriate sharing of data for public benefit. It ends by saying the strategy will produce concrete actions and results between 2020 and 2025.

sections.extract: through the application of digital health technologies for consumers, health professionals, health care providers and industry towards empowering patients and achieving the vision of health for all. The strategy is designed to be fit for purpose and for use by all Member States including those with limited access to digital technologies, goods and services. sections.title: Acknowledge that institutionalization of digital health in the national health system requires a decision and commitment by countries

summary.text: States the guiding principle that each country owns its digital health action plan and will adopt digital health in line with its own context and resources.

sections.extract: national health system requires a decision and commitment by countries The global strategy acknowledges that each country owns its digital health action plan built on the strategy, within its own national context. Along their path towards the health-related Sustainable Development Goals, countries will adopt digital health in a way that is sustainable, respects their sovereignty, and best suits their culture and

sections.title: Recognize that successful digital health initiatives require an integrated strategy

summary.text: Explains that digital health initiatives need an integrated, costed strategy with strong governance, standards and architecture. It warns that poorly coordinated initiatives lead to fragmented stand-alone systems.

sections.extract: integrated strategy Digital technologies are an essential component and an enabler of sustainable health systems and universal health coverage. To realize their potential, digital health initiatives must be part of the wider health needs and the digital health ecosystem and guided by a robust strategy that integrates leadership, financial, organizational, human and technological resources and is used as the basis

summary.text: A heading fragment introducing the four guiding principles.

sections.title: Promote the appropriate use of digital technologies for health

summary.text: Presents the principle of appropriate use of digital technologies as digital public goods, with protection from misinformation, cyber threats and misuse of health data. It notes the importance of digital determinants of health and lists qualities that appropriate digital health should have, including managing digital waste.

sections.extract: The global strategy promotes the appropriate use of digital technologies as digital public goods which are adaptable to different countries and contexts to help address key health system challenges to support equity in access to digital resources so that no one is left behind. It promotes the protection of people, populations, health care professionals and systems against misinformation and the misuse of

sections.title: Recognize the urgent need to address the major impediments faced by least-developed countries implementing digital health technologies

summary.text: States the principle that investment is urgently needed to overcome barriers faced by least-developed countries, such as infrastructure, skills, finance, connectivity and standards.

sections.extract: faced by least-developed countries implementing digital health technologies There is a pressing need to invest in efforts to overcome the major impediments that developing countries face in engaging with and accessing new digital health technologies, such as an appropriate enabling environment, sufficient resources, infrastructure to support the digital transformation, education, human capacity, financial investment

sections.title: Promote global collaboration and advance the transfer of knowledge on digital health

summary.text: Introduces strategic objective 1 on global collaboration and knowledge transfer, aiming to align countries and stakeholders on shared opportunities and risks. It covers maximizing partnerships and assessing new health technologies with norms and standards.

sections.extract: knowledge on digital health This strategic objective aims to align countries and stakeholders to collectively act upon global opportunities to improve health and work towards universal health coverage, while meeting challenges, identifying and communicating risks, and focusing on threats associated with the use of digital technologies both to improve health and to enable universal health coverage, the core of the

sections.title: STRATEGIC OBJECTIVES

summary.text: Introduces the four strategic objectives and lists policy options for objective 1, such as co-creating the strategy and knowledge management. It begins the expected outputs, including governance mechanisms and regular multistakeholder groups.

sections.extract: coordination on global digital health transformation and to strengthen synergies between initiatives and stakeholders to improve health outcomes and mitigate associated risks at all levels. sections.title: Advance the implementation of national digital health strategies

summary.text: Describes strategic objective 2 on helping each country own and strengthen a national digital health strategy, with core components from leadership and investment to standards and interoperability. It lists policy options such as stakeholder engagement, a national roadmap, open data standards and legal and ethical frameworks for patient safety and data security.

sections.extract: strategies Strategic objective 2 aims to stimulate and support every country to own, adapt and strengthen its strategy on digital health in a way that best suits its vision, national context, health situation and trends, available resources and core values. Strategic objective 2 encourages the development of a national strategy on digital health through an all- inclusive multistakeholder approach including actors

sections.title: Strengthen governance for digital health at global, regional and national levels

summary.text: Describes strategic objective 3 on strengthening digital health governance and capacity, with standards for security, privacy, interoperability and ethical data use and a research agenda. It lists policy options and outputs such as a health data regulatory framework and voluntary interoperability guidance. It ends with guidance on digital hospitals and recommendations on pseudonymizing and anonymizing health data.

sections.extract: national levels This strategic objective focuses on strengthening the governance of digital health at national and international levels through the creation of sustainable and robust governance structures and building the capacity for digital health at global and national levels. Governance for digital health aims to strengthen the capabilities and skills needed for countries to promote, innovate and scale up

sections.title: Advocate people-centred health systems that are enabled by digital health

summary.text: Describes strategic objective 4 on people-centred health systems enabled by digital health, covering digital literacy, gender equality and readiness of health workers. It lists policy options on population health management, public participation and training. Outputs include global minimum health data standards and guidance on personalized medicine.

sections.extract: digital health This strategic objective advances digital health literacy, gender equality and women’s empowerment and inclusive approaches to adoption and management of digital health technologies. The strategic objective places people at the centre of digital health through the adoption and use of digital health technologies in scaling up and strengthening health service delivery. sections.title: Commit

summary.text: Describes the commit component of the framework for action, asking countries and stakeholders to make voluntary commitments to implement the strategy.

sections.extract: Encourage countries and stakeholders to commit themselves to the implementation of the global strategy on digital health. In order to reach the strategic objectives of the global strategy, the Secretariat, Member States and stakeholders shall maintain their voluntary commitment and contributions, respecting national priorities, capabilities and resources.

sections.title: Catalyse

summary.text: Describes the catalyse component, creating a cooperative environment for scaling up digital health technologies, with the Secretariat promoting collaboration.

sections.extract: Generate and sustain a conducive environment to create, scale up and maintain processes that will facilitate collaboration towards implementing the global strategy. This component envisages the generation of a cooperative environment that is conducive to the creation, introduction and scaling up of appropriate digital health technologies and enabling processes that will facilitate and accelerate the implementation

sections.title: FRAMEWORK FOR ACTION

summary.text: Explains that the framework for action provides structure and tools for collaboration, guided by four components and accompanied by an action plan for each strategic objective.

sections.extract: The framework for action aims to facilitate the implementation of the global strategy by providing a structure and tools for collaboration. Working collectively towards shared strategic objectives, local and global partners can accommodate diversity and jointly consider concepts, road maps, methods, tools, funding and other factors to help implementation and support countries in various development contexts to make

sections.title: Measure

summary.text: Describes the measure component, under which the Secretariat will assess the strategy's effectiveness from global data and report to Member States.

sections.extract: Create and adopt processes and metrics for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of the global strategy. This component calls for the continuous assessment of whether the global strategy on digital health has been true to its purpose and effective in supporting countries. The Secretariat will measure the effectiveness of the global strategy from data collected globally and will report findings to Member States.

sections.title: Enhance and iterate

summary.text: Describes the enhance and iterate component, with annual review of the action plan to decide on new cycles of action. It also notes collaboration on quality-assured digital global public goods.

sections.extract: Undertake a new cycle of actions based on what has been experienced, measured and learned. This component will respond to feedback on the progress of global strategy in adapting to emerging digital health technologies. The action plan will be reviewed annually to determine whether a new cycle of new actions is needed to deliver on the strategic objectives. sections.title: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE STRATEGY AND ACTION PLAN

summary.text: Introduces implementation of the strategy and action plan in line with country health priorities, universal health coverage and WHO's Thirteenth General Programme of Work, with a summary figure.

sections.extract: AND ACTION PLAN The global strategy on digital health aims to support and respond to the growing needs of countries to implement appropriate digital technologies in accordance with their health priorities and to make progress towards universal health coverage and the health-related Sustainable Development Goals. It also responds to the objectives of WHO’s Thirteenth General Programme of Work, 2019–2023. Figure 1

sections.title: General implementation principles

summary.text: Sets out general principles for implementing the strategy with Member States and many stakeholders, with timelines, milestones and core process indicators. It discusses financing needs and stresses that countries should choose actions suited to their digital health maturity. It notes that the annex describes short-, medium- and long-term actions and that progress will be reported to the Assembly.

sections.extract: implementation principles The Secretariat will work closely with Member States, other bodies in the United Nations system, international partners and other stakeholders to implement the global strategy. It is intended that various stakeholders will take the strategic objectives forward at national, regional and global levels. sections.title: Specific implementation principles

summary.text: Sets out specific principles for a national interoperable digital health ecosystem based on agreed use cases, standards and a sound legal framework. It covers protecting health data, digital identification and a coordinated approach to the economics of health data.

sections.extract: implementation principles A national interoperable digital health ecosystem should be set up in such a way that the information technology health infrastructures are both interoperable among each other and, allowing for differences in national legislation and policies, capable of sharing health data with infrastructures of other countries. sections.title: MONITORING AND EVALUATION

summary.text: Describes monitoring and evaluation through standard metrics on digital health maturity and a value measurement model, while minimizing extra data burdens. Based on the shown end, the block also begins the glossary with definitions such as digital divide and digital health.

sections.extract: The action plan calls for Member States and the Secretariat to dynamically monitor the maturity level of digital health in countries and institutions and to assess the implementation of digital health strategies through standard agreed-upon metrics. These measures should include both the status and performance of digital health interventions and include established monitoring and evaluation models to facilitate

sections.title: GLOSSARY

summary.text: The glossary of the digital health strategy, defining terms such as artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, digital health, infodemic, interoperability and telemedicine, with source notes. It is followed by the annex setting out proposed actions for Member States, the Secretariat and partners. The annex is organized by the four strategic objectives and by short-, medium- and long-term time frames. The end lists actions under objective 4 on people-centred health systems, such as supporting interoperable digital systems to improve quality, coverage and access.

narratives.en: Figure 1, a colour-coded framework summarizing implementation of the action plan, with columns Objectives, Outcomes, Outputs, Policy & Action and Target impacts. Each strategic objective forms a row: SO1 Collaboration and knowledge transfer → global alignment to address opportunities and challenges → increasingly appropriate and sustainable digital health ecosystem; SO2 Digital strategy implementation → strategic vision and integrated action at the national level → cost-effective and efficient health systems and services; SO3 Digital health governance → actions and investments based on informed decisions → accelerated digitalization of the health and well-being sector; SO4 Human-centred health systems → people empowered to make healthy and health-enabling choices → healthier populations. Each row also lists three outputs and four policy and action areas.
narratives.ar: الشكل 1، إطار مرمّز بالألوان يلخّص تنفيذ خطة العمل، بأعمدة: الأهداف، والحصائل، والنواتج، والسياسات والإجراءات، والآثار المستهدفة. يشكّل كل هدف استراتيجي صفاً: الهدف الاستراتيجي 1 التعاون ونقل المعارف ← المواءمة العالمية لمعالجة الفرص والتحديات ← منظومة صحة رقمية ملائمة ومستدامة على نحو متزايد؛ الهدف الاستراتيجي 2 تنفيذ الاستراتيجية الرقمية ← رؤية استراتيجية وعمل متكامل على الصعيد الوطني ← نظم وخدمات صحية فعالة من حيث التكلفة وكفؤة؛ الهدف الاستراتيجي 3 حوكمة الصحة الرقمية ← إجراءات واستثمارات قائمة على قرارات مستنيرة ← تسريع رقمنة قطاع الصحة والعافية؛ الهدف الاستراتيجي 4 نظم صحية محورها الإنسان ← تمكين الناس من اتخاذ خيارات صحية ومعزِّزة للصحة ← سكان أوفر صحة. ويدرج كل صف أيضاً ثلاثة نواتج وأربعة مجالات للسياسات والإجراءات.
narratives.zh: 图1：以颜色区分的框架，概述行动计划的实施，各列为目标、成果、产出、政策与行动以及目标影响。每个战略目标构成一行：战略目标1 协作与知识转让 → 在全球层面协调一致以应对机遇和挑战 → 日益适宜且可持续的数字卫生生态系统；战略目标2 数字战略实施 → 国家层面的战略愿景和综合行动 → 具有成本效益且高效的卫生系统和服务；战略目标3 数字卫生治理 → 基于知情决策的行动和投资 → 加速卫生和福祉部门的数字化；战略目标4 以人为本的卫生系统 → 增强人们作出健康和有利于健康之选择的能力 → 更健康的人群。每行还列出三项产出和四个政策与行动领域。
narratives.es: Figura 1: marco codificado por colores que resume la aplicación del plan de acción, con las columnas Objetivos, Resultados, Productos, Políticas y acciones e Impactos previstos. Cada objetivo estratégico forma una fila: OE1 Colaboración y transferencia de conocimientos → armonización mundial para abordar oportunidades y desafíos → ecosistema de salud digital cada vez más adecuado y sostenible; OE2 Aplicación de la estrategia digital → visión estratégica y acción integrada a nivel nacional → sistemas y servicios de salud costoeficaces y eficientes; OE3 Gobernanza de la salud digital → acciones e inversiones basadas en decisiones informadas → digitalización acelerada del sector de la salud y el bienestar; OE4 Sistemas de salud centrados en las personas → personas empoderadas para tomar decisiones saludables y propicias para la salud → poblaciones más sanas. Cada fila enumera además tres productos y cuatro ámbitos de políticas y acción.
narratives.fr: Figure 1 : cadre codé par couleurs résumant la mise en œuvre du plan d’action, avec les colonnes Objectifs, Résultats, Produits, Politiques et action et Impacts visés. Chaque objectif stratégique forme une ligne : OS1 Collaboration et transfert de connaissances → alignement mondial pour faire face aux possibilités et aux défis → écosystème de santé numérique de plus en plus approprié et durable ; OS2 Mise en œuvre de la stratégie numérique → vision stratégique et action intégrée au niveau national → systèmes et services de santé efficients et d’un bon rapport coût/efficacité ; OS3 Gouvernance de la santé numérique → actions et investissements fondés sur des décisions éclairées → numérisation accélérée du secteur de la santé et du bien-être ; OS4 Systèmes de santé centrés sur la personne → personnes habilitées à faire des choix sains et favorables à la santé → populations en meilleure santé. Chaque ligne énumère aussi trois produits et quatre domaines de politique et d’action.
narratives.ru: Рисунок 1: цветовая схема, обобщающая осуществление плана действий, со столбцами «Цели», «Конечные результаты», «Промежуточные результаты», «Политика и действия» и «Целевое воздействие». Каждая стратегическая цель образует строку: СЦ1 «Сотрудничество и передача знаний» → глобальная согласованность в использовании возможностей и решении проблем → всё более адекватная и устойчивая экосистема цифрового здравоохранения; СЦ2 «Реализация цифровой стратегии» → стратегическое видение и комплексные действия на национальном уровне → экономически эффективные и действенные системы и услуги здравоохранения; СЦ3 «Руководство цифровым здравоохранением» → действия и инвестиции на основе обоснованных решений → ускоренная цифровизация сектора здоровья и благополучия; СЦ4 «Системы здравоохранения, ориентированные на человека» → люди, способные делать здоровый и благоприятствующий здоровью выбор → более здоровое население. В каждой строке также перечислены три промежуточных результата и четыре направления политики и действий.

narratives.en: Photograph of a woman holding a smartphone against a small round sensor worn on her upper arm; the phone screen shows a glucose reading of 5.10 marked “normal”.
narratives.ar: صورة فوتوغرافية لامرأة تمسك هاتفاً ذكياً بالقرب من مستشعر دائري صغير مثبت على أعلى ذراعها؛ وتعرض شاشة الهاتف قراءة للغلوكوز قدرها 5.10 مع عبارة "طبيعي".
narratives.zh: 照片：一名女性将智能手机靠近佩戴在上臂的小型圆形传感器；手机屏幕显示血糖读数5.10，标注为“正常”。
narratives.es: Fotografía de una mujer que acerca un teléfono inteligente a un pequeño sensor redondo colocado en la parte superior del brazo; la pantalla muestra una lectura de glucosa de 5,10 marcada como «normal».
narratives.fr: Photographie d’une femme tenant un smartphone contre un petit capteur rond porté sur le haut du bras ; l’écran affiche une glycémie de 5,10 marquée « normale ».
narratives.ru: Фотография: женщина подносит смартфон к небольшому круглому датчику на плече; на экране телефона отображается уровень глюкозы 5,10 с пометкой «норма».

narratives.en: Photograph of a health worker wearing a headscarf, face mask, gloves and a vest bearing the WHO emblem, writing with a pen in a handwritten paper register.
narratives.ar: صورة فوتوغرافية لعاملة صحية ترتدي غطاء رأس وكمامة وجه وقفازات وسترة تحمل شعار منظمة الصحة العالمية، وهي تكتب بقلم في سجل ورقي مكتوب بخط اليد.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名戴头巾、口罩和手套、身穿印有世卫组织标志背心的卫生工作者，正用笔在手写纸质登记簿上书写。
narratives.es: Fotografía de una trabajadora de salud con pañuelo en la cabeza, mascarilla, guantes y un chaleco con el emblema de la OMS, que escribe con un bolígrafo en un registro de papel manuscrito.
narratives.fr: Photographie d’une agente de santé portant un foulard, un masque, des gants et un gilet arborant l’emblème de l’OMS, qui écrit au stylo dans un registre papier manuscrit.
narratives.ru: Фотография: медицинский работник в платке, маске, перчатках и жилете с эмблемой ВОЗ делает записи ручкой в бумажном журнале регистрации.

narratives.en: Photograph of a child in a blue shirt wearing headphones and looking down at a tablet held in their hands, lit by the screen; another person in blue is partly visible on the left.
narratives.ar: صورة فوتوغرافية لطفل يرتدي قميصاً أزرق ويضع سماعات رأس وينظر إلى جهاز لوحي يمسكه بيديه، ويضيء وجهَه ضوءُ الشاشة؛ ويظهر جزء من شخص آخر يرتدي الأزرق على اليسار.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名身穿蓝色衬衫、戴着耳机的儿童低头看着手中的平板电脑，脸部被屏幕照亮；左侧可见另一名身穿蓝色衣服者的部分身影。
narratives.es: Fotografía de un niño con camisa azul y auriculares que mira una tableta que sostiene en las manos, iluminado por la pantalla; a la izquierda se ve parcialmente a otra persona vestida de azul.
narratives.fr: Photographie d'un enfant en chemise bleue portant un casque audio et regardant une tablette qu'il tient dans ses mains, éclairé par l'écran ; une autre personne vêtue de bleu est partiellement visible à gauche.
narratives.ru: Фотография ребенка в синей рубашке и наушниках, который смотрит на планшет в руках; лицо освещено экраном; слева частично виден другой человек в синем.

narratives.en: Photograph of a smiling boy in a red T-shirt holding a basic mobile phone, with a woman in a blue dress and patterned fabric partly visible behind him.
narratives.ar: صورة فوتوغرافية لصبي مبتسم يرتدي قميصاً أحمر ويمسك هاتفاً محمولاً بسيطاً، وتظهر خلفه جزئياً امرأة ترتدي ثوباً أزرق وقماشاً مزخرفاً.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名身穿红色T恤、面带微笑的男孩手持一部普通手机，身后可见一名穿蓝色连衣裙的妇女和带图案的布料的部分身影。
narratives.es: Fotografía de un niño sonriente con camiseta roja que sostiene un teléfono móvil básico; detrás se ve parcialmente a una mujer con vestido azul y una tela estampada.
narratives.fr: Photographie d'un garçon souriant en T-shirt rouge tenant un téléphone portable basique ; derrière lui, une femme en robe bleue et un tissu à motifs sont partiellement visibles.
narratives.ru: Фотография улыбающегося мальчика в красной футболке с простым мобильным телефоном в руках; позади частично видны женщина в синем платье и ткань с узором.
